problems.title: The released success path does not enforce preservation of the requested theorem
problems.source_location: Section 3.3, PDF pp. 4–5; Section 5.1, PDF p. 5; released Prove.run and verifier.
claim: Sections 3.3 and \(5.1\), PDF pp. 4–5, describe completing the requested proof and verifying it with Lean 4. Released dsp/prove.py, check_proof, warns when the requested theorem is changed or commented out, but run can still mark an otherwise error-free, sorry-free returned program as finished; run_direct returns the underlying completion result without enforcing target identity.
analysis: An unrelated declaration proving True can be error-free and sorry-free without proving a requested False statement. A target-mismatch warning that does not block the success branch therefore fails to enforce theorem identity. This is a controller-contract argument; no false Lean theorem or actual kernel acceptance of a false proposition is claimed.

Placing the exact requested target text inside a Lean block comment also passes the whitespace-substring check. Thus elevating the existing warning alone would not repair target preservation. These are conditional controller witnesses using a successful compiler-response interface, not claims of a newly compiled proof.
result: The current controller can accept a different completed declaration, but no actual target mismatch was found in the historical released-solution inventory and no benchmark score is revised.
repair: Keep the target declaration immutable and restrict generation/repair to its proof body. Make acceptance depend on compiler-aware declaration name/type/assumption and admitted-axiom checks; a comment-stripping specimen guard is not a complete Lean parser.
problems.impact_rationale: The current controller can accept a different completed declaration, but no actual target mismatch was found in the historical released-solution inventory and no benchmark score is revised.
problems.existing_correction_status: A local correction or qualification is proposed where specified; author adoption is not established.

problems.title: The unrestricted-hypothesis fallback is inactive by default and fails when enabled
problems.source_location: Appendix A.1, PDF p. 21; released fallback send_request.
claim: Appendix A.1, PDF p. 21, describes both hinted-hypothesis and unrestricted-context proof search. In the released proving interface, run and run_direct leave the strict retry disabled by default; its enabled branch calls send_request without a required argument.
analysis: Normal calls leave the strict flag false, so the unrestricted retry is not reached. Enabling it exposes a missing required send_request argument and fails before the request. Both mechanisms are version-bounded control-flow/interface defects; their benchmark incidence is unmeasured.
result: The current fallback is unreachable under default calls and raises a missing-argument error when enabled; search coverage changes, without invalidating accepted Lean proofs.
repair: Pass both proof blocks and the current bfs_list to the retry, and explicitly enable the intended fallback policy. This restores the local interface, without establishing an improved theorem-proving success rate.
problems.impact_rationale: The current fallback is unreachable under default calls and raises a missing-argument error when enabled; search coverage changes, without invalidating accepted Lean proofs.
problems.existing_correction_status: A local correction or qualification is proposed where specified; author adoption is not established.

problems.title: Reproduction of the authors’ known logarithm-domain issue in miniF2F
problems.source_location: Appendix F, PDF pp. 27–28 (known nested-logarithm contest formalization).
claim: Appendix F, PDF pp. 27–28, already diagnoses and corrects the original miniF2F nested-logarithm formalization. The inspected author dataset contains the strengthened domain condition. No discovery credit is claimed.
analysis: Under Lean's totalized Real.logb convention, \(n=1\) makes both nested logarithms zero and satisfies the original formal equation, while its decimal digit sum is \(1\), not \(13\). The informal contest problem's positive logarithm domains exclude this endpoint. This reproduces the authors' disclosed formalization issue.

The current author dataset explicitly requires \(1<n\), excluding this witness. On that domain, writing \(t=\log_2 n>0\) reduces the equation to \(\log_2t-2=(\log_2t-1)/2\), hence \(n=256\) and digit sum \(13\).
result: The author-disclosed historical domain error is corrected in the current dataset. It is retained as history and supplies no current issue severity.
problems.impact_rationale: Current domain \(1<n\) excludes the exact historical boundary; this concern is already corrected and is not counted as an active error.
problems.existing_correction_status: The authors already diagnose this domain issue in Appendix F, and the inspected dataset includes their strengthened condition. No new correction or priority is claimed.

impact_rationale: The two current controller/search defects remain bounded to the released implementation. The historical dataset-domain concern is cleared, and no false Lean theorem or inflated published score is established.
